title: Hegseth falsely claims Obama called 2009 Fort Hood attack ‘workplace violence’ – US politics live
text: 20.14 EDT Hegseth falsely claims Obama called 2009 Fort Hood attack 'workplace violence' In an interview on Thursday with the rightwing network Real America’s Voice, Pete Hegseth, the US defense secretary, joined Donald Trump in trying to use the 2009 shooting rampage at Fort Hood in Texas to attack former president Barack Obama. On Wednesday night, Trump made the wildly false claim that Obama had emails from the attacker describing his plans in advance but chose not to stop him. Speaking on Thursday to the far-right influencer Jack Posobiec, who helped spread the debunked Pizzagate conspiracy theory to smear Democrats in 2016, the defense secretary announced that Nidal Hasan, the former army psychiatrist who killed 12 soldiers and one civilian at Fort Hood, would be executed by firing squad later this year. Hegseth, a former Fox News host, then falsely claimed that Obama had downplayed the attack. “It was a radical Islamist terror attack,” Hegseth said. “Remember what Obama called it? ‘Workplace violence,’” the defense secretary said, falsely, as Posobiec nodded vigorously. “I mean, that’s what we’re up against. title: ICE agent shoots man in New York City with five-year-old in car, mayor says
text: A protester holds a sign in the Bronx after the ICE shooting. Zohran Mamdani, the mayor, said he had called the president. Photograph: Eduardo Muñoz/Reuters View image in fullscreen A protester holds a sign in the Bronx after the ICE shooting. Zohran Mamdani, the mayor, said he had called the president. Photograph: Eduardo Muñoz/Reuters New York ICE agent shoots man in New York City with five-year-old in car, mayor says Police say man taken to hospital and mayor says child physically unharmed as he condemns ‘unconscionable’ act Sam Levin Thu 8 Oct 2026 20.13 EDT First published on Thu 8 Oct 2026 18.35 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent shot a man in New York City on Thursday afternoon, according to the city’s mayor, Zohran Mamdani. Early reports indicated that agents had surrounded the man and a five-year-old child in his car in a residential area before firing multiple rounds, the mayor said in a statement on Thursday evening. The child was physically unharmed, according to Mamdani. The individual who was shot was conscious and taken to a hospital, the NYPD said in a brief statement .
